title: What Happened in the Experiment?
pedagogicalStatus: Unreviewed draft: formative practice only; CEFR mastery disabled.

sources.title: Pendulum observation diary (reading; practice)
paragraphs: On Monday, Lina watched a pendulum in a classroom video. She started a timer and counted ten complete oscillations. In the first trial, the timer showed 14.8 seconds. She repeated the video measurement and recorded 15.0 seconds in the second trial. Lina wrote both numbers in her notebook. She did not change the length of the pendulum. She checked the table and sent the results to her lab partner. This was a learning activity using recorded video, not a claim about a physical laboratory experiment.

sources.title: Virtual circuit notebook (reading; practice)
paragraphs: Yesterday, Omar opened a circuit simulation. He chose a resistor and set the virtual source to 6.0 V. The screen showed a current of 0.12 A. Omar read the value, took a screenshot, and saved a graph. He did not connect any real wires. At the end, he wrote: "The virtual current was 0.12 A." The numbers belong to this fictional simulation record, not to an official lab handout.

sources.title: Optics class log (reading; practice)
paragraphs: Last Thursday, Maya examined three simple ray diagrams. First, she marked the lens position. Then she drew one horizontal incident ray and its refracted path in a model drawing. After that, she compared the first diagram with the second. She found two different image positions. She did not use a real laser or any other optical apparatus. Finally, she wrote a short description of the diagrams.

sources.title: Temperature-simulation record (reading; practice)
paragraphs: Two days ago, a group observed a computer model of a warming object. At the beginning, the display read 21.0 °C. Four minutes later, it read 25.0 °C. The students recorded the two readings and calculated a difference of 4.0 °C. They did not touch a hot object. Their teacher asked, "Did the simulated temperature increase?" They answered yes and explained that the later reading was higher.
